ranked.headline: Graph-based autoencoders advance unsupervised single-cell and spatial omics analysis
ranked.summary: Recent publications extend graph neural networks and autoencoders to scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomic and single-cell Hi-C data.

ranked.headline: Statistical frameworks target replicability and robustness in multi-omics inference
ranked.summary: Recent work tests whether omics biomarkers and associations hold across cohorts, subgroups, and independent studies rather than single datasets.

ranked.headline: Pretrained sequence models guide generative design of peptides, nanobodies, and PROTACs
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs pretrained protein and molecule language models with preference, surrogate, and developability objectives for targeted design.

ranked.headline: Contrastive and graph learning align multi-omics and spatial transcriptomics data
ranked.summary: Unpaired single-cell and spatial modalities now demand integration methods that add interpretability and explicit cross-modal alignment.

ranked.headline: Learned models fuse graphs, LLM embeddings and protein sequences for molecular design
ranked.summary: Knowledge graphs, LLM reasoning and geometric or target-level structure are now being built into perturbation, drug response and lead-optimization models.

ranked.headline: Ensemble and network methods extract gene modules and subtypes from transcriptomic data
ranked.summary: Recent methods extend co-expression networks, ensemble clustering and single-cell evaluation to disease-relevant transcriptomic and spatial data.

ranked.headline: Dynamical models link brain morphology, connectivity and amyloid-β trajectories
ranked.summary: Joint cohort calibration and multimodal longitudinal data now let dynamic models test shared spatiotemporal and genetic structure in brain change.

ranked.headline: ML frameworks align and segment spatial omics and multimodal microscopy data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers apply learned and physics-based models to segment, unmix, register, and virtually stain multimodal spatial and optical data.

ranked.headline: Long-read assemblies yield chromosome-scale genomes across diverse eukaryotic lineages
ranked.summary: Long-read and chromatin-conformation data now yield reference genomes with high BUSCO completeness across diverse lineages.

ranked.headline: Software pipelines formalize QC, reproducibility and benchmarking in sequencing analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications extend sequencing analysis tools to GPU-accelerated GWAS, duplex sequencing, and long-read structural variant calling.

ranked.headline: LLM agents and AI methods are being applied to spatial omics and genomics analysis
ranked.summary: Proprietary LLM dependence and reproducibility concerns sit alongside new viewer-grounded agentic tools for spatial omics analysis.

ranked.headline: Multi-organ and module-resolved clocks decompose individual biological aging state
ranked.summary: Preprints and publications apply proteomic and multi-omic profiles to resolve per-individual aging state and disease-associated deviation.

ranked.headline: Deep models infer gene regulation and predict in-silico perturbation outcomes
ranked.summary: Single-cell foundation models and transformers now target gene regulatory and perturbation inference, with explicit generalization tests.

ranked.headline: Computational design of sequences for defined folds, motifs, and nucleic acid structures
ranked.summary: Generative and energy-based design methods now target peptides, Rossmann folds, and RNA, with AlphaFold-based screening as the verification step.

ranked.headline: Protein language model embeddings extended with dynamics, structure, and text semantics
ranked.summary: Recent items pair ESM-family and ProtT5 embeddings with conformational dynamics, residue-level structure graphs, and partner-aware modeling for PPI site…

ranked.headline: Annotation-light models infer microbial pathogenicity, viral origins, and gene order
ranked.summary: Annotation-free and taxonomy-agnostic models are extending genomic inference beyond reference-dependent annotation pipelines.

ranked.headline: Adhesion and drug effects drive emergent spatial organization in tissues and tumours
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple mechanistic adhesion, migration and drug-response models to spatial patterns in growing, invading and treated populations.

ranked.headline: Deep models predict protein function, design sequences and map reaction transformations
ranked.summary: Pretrained language-model representations are being paired with structure, text, graph and prior information to handle low-homology, zero-shot and data-limited…

ranked.headline: Compact formalisms probe how noise, spatial structure and network weighting govern…
ranked.summary: Compact formalisms now probe how noise, spatial structure and network weighting govern emergent states in gene, multicellular and neural systems.

ranked.headline: Learned models predict TCR-pMHC recognition and epitope immunogenicity
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and frameworks test how sequence, structure, and language models capture immune receptor and epitope recognition.

ranked.headline: Regulatory chromatin read at kilobase to nucleosome and repeat resolution
ranked.summary: Methods now resolve methylation, accessibility, and 3D contacts at single-cell and spatial scales, tying regulatory activity to its genomic context.

ranked.headline: Cross-platform spatial transcriptomics benchmarked against shared matched references
ranked.summary: Xenium off-target probe binding and platform noise now motivate matched-reference evaluation of spatial transcriptomics assays.

ranked.headline: Sequence representations drive pathogen resistance and antigenicity prediction
ranked.summary: Pangenome-scale features and protein language model embeddings are being benchmarked for resistance and antigenic site prediction.

ranked.headline: AlphaFold2 and graph-based encoders as learned features for molecular prediction tasks
ranked.summary: Structure-aware embeddings and graph transformers are being applied across docking, stability, interface, and crystallization prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Foundation and language models tackle single-cell reasoning and sequencing metadata
Web and Shiny interfaces now expose spatial, methylation and multi-omics analyses
ranked.summary: Spatial, methylation, proteomic and multi-omics datasets are being packaged into Shiny apps, web servers and R packages for direct analysis.

ranked.headline: Open software tools extend phylogenetic inference and tree handling
ranked.summary: Recent releases add richer evolutionary models and accessible interfaces for tree inference, population structure detection, and tree digitization.

ranked.headline: Learned models regress geometry and complete missing spatial data, bypassing masks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints shift from purely mask-based prediction toward direct regression of geometry and generative completion of spatial data.

ranked.headline: In silico tools score docking poses, ADME, and peptide structures before wet-lab work
ranked.summary: Reproducibility and explicit intermediate criteria are becoming central to open-source pre-experimental design software.

ranked.headline: Learned models span RNA and protein design, folding, and coding-sequence annotation
ranked.summary: Three preprints and one published study from early May 2026 extend learned sequence and structure models across RNA design, folding, and ensemble inference.

ranked.headline: Workflows drop assembly or control dependencies in viral and metagenomic analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications describe open-source workflows for decontamination, viral phylogenetics, and quasispecies comparison from sequencing reads.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based methods increasingly encode local structural context in protein analysis
ranked.summary: Protein language models, fragment representations and structure-mapped pipelines now expose 3D context from sequence and variant data alone.

ranked.headline: Learned models resolve RNA regulatory features from single-cell and spatial data
ranked.summary: Deep learning and interpretable models now extract cell-type, isoform, polyadenylation and modification signals from single-cell and spatial RNA data.

ranked.headline: Modular software for microbial genome recovery, classification, and benchmarking
ranked.summary: Recent items package MAG recovery, strain-level hybrid workflows, and benchmarking as open, reproducible tools for microbial genomics.

ranked.headline: Parallel and memory-efficient redesigns of alignment and indexing for sequencing data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications report GPU, SIMD, and linear-space redesigns that cut memory or runtime in core sequence computations.

ranked.headline: GWAS and omic features feeding predictive models for disease and therapeutic targets
ranked.summary: Benchmarks and new frameworks now test whether genetic and multi-omic inputs improve prediction of disease and biomarker outcomes.

ranked.headline: Selection inference is moving from sequence to predicted molecular function
ranked.summary: Function-level selection tests and primate-wide simulation evidence for linked selection are now reshaping how genome-wide selection is inferred.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and pipelines for long-read and single-cell RNA-seq analysis
ranked.summary: Long-read and single-cell RNA-seq tools now address variant calling, isoform reconstruction, HLA typing, and workflow reproducibility.

ranked.headline: Structural and model constraints sharpen noninvasive mapping of brain dynamics
ranked.summary: Constraining noninvasive brain models with cortical geometry and interpretable structure now shows both reconstruction gains and clear limits on transfer.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking and ion-level refinement of DIA and MS/MS proteomics software
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published method target missing-value handling, low-input DIA libraries, and standardized evaluation of spectrum prediction tools.
